subject: Re: Plan to convert commit to tiered slab pools and utilization smoothing
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Li <sarah@scalarize.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conversion proposal: commit -> tiered slab pools for Q3

Tessa / team,

Quick note following our call this morning with Sarah at Scalarize. They saw a sustained 42% utilization on their committed A100 tranche over the last 60 days, with short peaks up to 78% during nightly batch jobs. Their renewal (DEAL-4521) is due in late July and they asked whether we can convert the remaining committed tranche into a tiered slab allocation to smooth bursts and reduce overprovisioning.

Proposed high-level:
- Convert 12 committed GPUs into a 3-tier slab: steady (6 GPUs), buffer (3 GPUs, pre-warmed), burst (3 GPUs, on-demand uplift within commit window)
- Add automated utilization smoothing (dynamic rebalancer) and prefix/KV caching to reduce peak token costs
- Phased rollout: pilot for 30 days on a dedicated namespace, then scale to full tenancy on sign-off

Attachments: proposed_slab_layout.pdf (diagram, one page)

As next steps I recommend:
1) Tessa/Karthik—run a quick sim against Scalarize Q1 logs to validate expected token-hour savings (they volunteered CSV)
2) Jordan—put together an SOW draft with pricing tiers for steady + buffer + burst and crediting options for first-month migration risk
3) If results look positive, offer a 6-week conversion window at a transitional price to secure renewal

Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Li <sarah@scalarize.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conversion proposal: commit -> tiered slab pools for Q3

Thanks Ben — good synopsis.

Karthik: can you ingest the CSV Sarah attached in the portal and run the utilization sim? Focus on:
- 95th percentile sustained GPU occupancy per week
- Percent of run-hours where KV-cache hit rate drops below 60% (that will drive burst needs)
- Expected token-hour reduction with a 2x prefix cache hit improvement

Sarah — received the CSV (scalarize_utilization_q1.csv). We’ll run the sim by EOD Thursday and share a short one-page ROI showing the expected unit cost reduction and latency impact.

Jordan — please start a SOW skeleton. We should include an option: convert now with 2 weeks free buffer capacity, or convert on renewal with a 3-month credit ramp. Pricing table should show steady/buffer/burst hourly rates and an estimated monthly blended unit cost.

Attachments: scalarize_utilization_q1.csv (customer-supplied usage logs)

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan | Strategic Accounts Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sarah Li <sarah@scalarize.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conversion proposal: commit -> tiered slab pools for Q3

On Tue, Jun 29, 2027 at 10:03 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — good synopsis.
>
> Karthik: can you ingest the CSV Sarah attached in the portal and run the utilization sim? Focus on:
> - 95th percentile sustained GPU occupancy per week
> - Percent of run-hours where KV-cache hit rate drops below 60% (that will drive burst needs)
> - Expected token-hour reduction with a 2x prefix cache hit improvement

Quick simulation results (attached in summary below). I used the last 90 days of token/timestep logs and modeled three scenarios: baseline (no tiering), slab-conversion with 6/3/3 split, and slab + cache improvements.

Highlights:
- Baseline blended cost per token-hour: baseline_unit:$0.117 (normalized)
- Slab 6/3/3 reduces expected steady provisioning by ~28% and lowers average latency for interactive calls by 12ms
- Slab + cache improvements yields ~36% reduction in token-hour spend (driven by reduced burst hours and fewer cold-starts)
- Peak risk window: 0200–0430 UTC daily (batch jobs) — recommend a temporary scheduled pre-warm for 30 minutes before start to reduce burst latency and cold-start overhead

Attachments included in this message: proposed_slab_layout.pdf (design) and a short CSV of the sim summary.

If acceptable, I recommend:
- Pilot: provision 3 steady GPUs and 2 buffer GPUs for the namespace, with ability to bridge 2 GPUs from dedicated commit during night batch window (automated).
- Commercial: tiered pricing with blended discount (6–12 month commitments reduce buffer hourly by 10%).

Karthik Iyer | Head of Dedicated Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Attachments: proposed_slab_layout.pdf, sim_summary_scalarize_q1.csv

From: Sarah Li <sarah@scalarize.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@scalarize.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conversion proposal: commit -> tiered slab pools for Q3

Thanks — the numbers look promising. A couple of notes from procurement: 
- We need a clear SLA on buffer availability during the nightly batch window (0200–0500 UTC). Any missed buffer supply will impact our SLAs to end customers.
- Please include sample language for credits if scheduled pre-warm fails twice in a month.
- Pricing: we prefer the 6-month blended commit option, but need the first-month migration credit to offset engineering churn.

If you can send a short SOW + redlineable contract by Monday PDT, we can push the renewal to a decision by mid-July.

Sarah Li
Head of Ops, Scalarize AI

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Scalarize conversion — exec summary & next steps

Team—internal recap to prep for Monday SOW delivery:

What: Convert part of Scalarize commit to a tiered slab pool (6 steady / 3 buffer / 3 burst) with automated smoothing and a scheduled nightly pre-warm (0200–0230 UTC).
Why: Simulation shows ~36% token-hour reduction with acceptable latency improvements; reduces steady overprovisioning while preserving peak capacity.
Risks: procurement needs explicit SLA language for buffer availability and a credit clause for repeated pre-warm failures. Also need to validate that Scalarize’s batch job does not shift peak outside planned window after conversion.

Action items: 
- Jordan: SOW draft + pricing table (due Mon EOD). Include optional 1-month migration credit and an escalated support window for the first 8 weeks.
- Karthik: instrument the temporary scheduled pre-warm and confirm monitoring hooks for buffer failures (due Mon AM).
- Ben/Tessa: prepare a short customer-facing deck that shows month 0 vs month 3 blended unit cost and expected latency delta (shared with Sarah).

I’ll escalate to our Renewals desk for final approval if the SOW includes the migration credit and a conservative buffer SLA.

Laura Bennett | Director, Renewals & Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
